Configure OpenAI as an LLM provider for agentgateway.

Configure [OpenAI](https://openai.com/) as an LLM provider in agentgateway.

Note

Don’t have an API key to an LLM provider? You can still try out how LLM traffic works in agentgateway by following the [httpbun guide](/docs/kubernetes/main/llm/providers/httpbun/). Httpbun provides a mock LLM API endpoint that is compatible with the OpenAI API for chat completions.

## Before you begin[](#before-you-begin)

[Install and set up an agentgateway proxy](/docs/kubernetes/main/quickstart/install/).

## Set up access to OpenAI[](#set-up-access-to-openai)

## Verify in the UI[](#verify-admin-ui)

You can also confirm that the proxy received your configuration in the read-only [UI](/docs/kubernetes/main/observability/ui/). In Kubernetes mode, the UI reflects the configuration that the agentgateway controller pushes to the proxy, so it is a quick way to check that your resources took effect.

1.  Forward port 15000 from the `agentgateway-proxy` deployment to your local machine.
    
2.  While the port-forward is running, open [http://localhost:15000/ui/](http://localhost:15000/ui/) in your browser.
    
3.  From the **Traffic** menu, click **Routes**. Find your route, and click the view (eye) icon in its row to inspect the route and backend details.

![](/img/agentgateway-ui-kube-route-llm-dark.png)
